questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere where they offered in depth courses for my field of interest.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university was slow to send out information regarding like place and time to meet,what material to get and so on. I found this to be super confusing in the beginning, as it was very different from what I'm used to at University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An orientation tour the week after the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: A lot of people try Airbnb. Haven't met a single short term exchange student who managed to find housing on campus so wouldn't bother too much looking into that.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Toronto is expensive especially if you wish to live downtown, so be sure to set a bit of money aside.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You choose courses later than you do in Denmark, and you have a much longer period, where you can drop them without further notice. Be aware that not all the courses you see on the UofT will be available for you as it changes from semester to semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I contacted the registrars office if I felt unsure of anything in the course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got some pretty neat classes, but the one I wanted the most, I didn't get because it wasn't offered in the semester I was going abroad. I would've wished I had known that earlier on.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress if it takes time to get the confirmation and all of that. I can be a bit of a process, but the professors know that people changes courses quite a bit in the first few weeks, and they do take this into account in their planning of the course material.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course material itself is easier compared to university of copenhagen, but the workburden is a lot greater due to many, many assignments, presentations and quizzes that you need to participate in throughout the semester. Also there's both a midterm and an exam, which also increases the workload and restricts the flexibility.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was in many was like that of UCPH, with the exception of the workload from the constant assessment.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: CSB328H1 F Animal Developmental Biology, HMB300H1 F Neurobiology of Behaviour, HMB360H1 F Neurogenomics and HMB310H1 F Laboratory in Neuroscience

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed all my courses, but I will say that Neurogenomics definitely stood out the most. It was absolute amazing, with a great prof as well. The Laboratory in Neuroscience was super exciting and the prof was nice, but the workload was crazy. Even the Canadians complained about the amount of work being like way to great for the amount of credits.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You need to pay a mandatory health fee called UHIP.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery are really expensive. Going out to eat is a bit less than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There lots of sport facilites and a bunch of club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use all the amazing sport facilities, and many of the outdoor clubs are great as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: NY is close, and also you can take the train to see other beautiful cities like Ottowa.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadians are as friendly as the stereotype.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing in due time, don't make a lot of plans outside of uni before you get an idea of the scheduele - uni is not very flexible like in Denmark and lastly sit next to people sitting alone in class and make small talk. It's super easy to gets friends here.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friends and new exciting academic challenges.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The work burden and the fixed scheduele. I was not pleased about that.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
